hook.line: Sooner or later you need to say what happened before something else: thank someone for coming, apologise for not calling, explain a regret. Spanish has a compact way to look back.

examples.es: Después de haber firmado, se arrepintió.
examples.en: After having signed, he regretted it.

examples.es: Después de haber hablado con Vale, Tomás se sintió mejor.
examples.en: After having spoken with Vale, Tomás felt better.

examples.es: Se fue sin haber terminado el café.
examples.en: He left without having finished the coffee.

examples.es: Por no haber estudiado, no pasó el examen.
examples.en: For not having studied, he didn't pass the exam.

rule:
You already know *he firmado* ("I have signed"). To look back from inside a phrase, put *haber* in its base form and add the *-do* form: *haber firmado*, *haber venido*, *haber comido*.

Use it after words that take the base form of a verb: *después de haber firmado*, *por haber venido*, *sin haber terminado*. For "not", *no* goes before *haber*: *por no haber llamado*.

It says the action was finished before the main verb. English often shortens this to "after signing", and Spanish can too (*después de firmar*), but *haber* makes "already done" explicit.
smallPrint: Teachers call *haber firmado* the perfect infinitive: the base form of the *he firmado* tense.

readAndPick.es: Después de haber firmado, se arrepintió.
options: Before signing, he regretted it.
After having signed, he regretted it.
After signing, he will regret it.
Thanks for not having come.
Thanks, I'm coming.
Thanks for having come.
Sorry for not having called.
Sorry for having called.
Sorry, I'll call.

readAndPick.es: Se fue sin haber terminado el café.
options: He left after having finished the coffee.
He left without having finished the coffee.
He left to finish the coffee.

readAndPick.es: Por no haber estudiado, no pasó el examen.
options: After studying, he passed the exam.
Because he studied, he didn't pass the exam.
For not having studied, he didn't pass the exam.

readAndPick.es: Después de haber hablado con Vale, Tomás se sintió mejor.
options: After having spoken with Vale, Tomás felt better.
Before speaking with Vale, Tomás felt better.
Because he didn't speak with Vale, Tomás felt better.

readAndPick.es: Después de haber comido, salimos a caminar.
options: Before eating, we went out for a walk.
After having eaten, we went out for a walk.
After having eaten, they went out for a walk.

readAndPick.es: Me alegro de haber conocido a Rosa.
options: I'm glad to meet Rosa.
I'm glad I didn't meet Rosa.
I'm glad to have met Rosa.
Sorry for having arrived late.
Sorry for not having arrived late.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *haber* or *he* and type the whole sentence: *Gracias por ___ venido.* (Thank you for having come.)
yourTurn.why: After *por* the verb stays in its base form, so *haber*, not *he*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Sorry for not having called.
Type in Spanish: After having eaten, we went out for a walk.
yourTurn.answer: Después de haber comido, salimos a caminar.
yourTurn.why: *Después de* plus *haber* plus the *-do* form says what was done first.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: He left without having finished the coffee. (a man)
yourTurn.answer: Se fue sin haber terminado el café.
accept: Él se fue sin haber terminado el café.
yourTurn.why: *Sin* is followed by the base form, so *sin haber terminado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: For not having studied, he didn't pass the exam.
yourTurn.answer: Por no haber estudiado, no pasó el examen.
accept: Por no haber estudiado, él no pasó el examen.
yourTurn.why: *Por no haber estudiado* gives the reason, one step back in time.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Vale: *Después de haber comido, salimos a caminar.* Say: After having spoken with Vale, Tomás felt better.
yourTurn.answer: Después de haber hablado con Vale, Tomás se sintió mejor.
yourTurn.why: Same frame, new verb: *hablado* is the *-do* form of *hablar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm glad to have met Rosa.
yourTurn.answer: Me alegro de haber conocido a Rosa.
yourTurn.why: *Me alegro de* is followed by the base form, so *de haber conocido*.

pitfalls.wrong: Después de haber firmar, se arrepintió.
pitfalls.right: Después de haber firmado, se arrepintió.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *haber*, the verb takes its *-do* ending: *firmado*.
Almost. After *por* the verb stays in its base form: *haber*, not *he*.
Almost. *No* goes before *haber*, not after it.

personal: Thank someone or say sorry for something real, starting with *Gracias por haber* or *Perdón por no haber*.
